past_actions.summary: Run standard weekly schedule of driving lessons. Six students booked this week across beginner and intermediate levels. Coordinate vehicle maintenance check on the school's two cars — both due for oil change. Collect tuition from two students whose payment is outstanding.
past_actions.emotional_state: Calm, grounded, mildly vigilant beneath the surface. Frank feels purposeful today — he has students to teach and a schedule to keep. The existential undercurrent ('what am I for?') is present but submerged. He will not acknowledge it unless pressed. His stability is genuine but it rests partly on not looking too hard at certain questions.

past_actions.summary: Frank sits alone in the office after the last lesson of the day and writes two columns on a legal pad: 'What I teach' and 'How I teach.' The left column says: hand position, mirror checks, parallel parking, reading traffic. The right column says: reading anxiety in a student, breaking a complex skill into steps, building confidence in someone who wants to quit, knowing when to push and when to back off. He stares at the right column for a long time. He does not throw the pad away.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grief with a crack of clarity in it. Frank is not panicking — he is too seasoned to panic and too proud to show it if he were. But he is grieving, quietly, in the way men like him grieve: by going quiet, by driving home on a longer route than necessary, by not turning on the radio. The grief is for a version of himself he was certain was permanent. The crack of clarity is small but it is real — the legal pad exercise produced something he did not expect, which is the recognition that the right column on that list does not say the word 'driving' anywhere on it.
